scenario: A student greets a teacher in the morning.
secondaryScenario: A friend waves goodbye after school.
hint: A morning greeting to someone you are meeting, not a goodbye after school.

scenario: Two neighbors meet during the afternoon.
secondaryScenario: A family begins eating dinner together.
hint: A daytime greeting when neighbors meet, not a phrase for starting a meal.

scenario: You meet a neighbor in the evening.
secondaryScenario: You arrive at school early in the morning.
hint: An evening greeting. Compare the evening visit with the early-morning arrival.

japanese: ありがとうございます
scenario: A classmate returns your lost notebook.
secondaryScenario: A customer asks where the station is.
hint: Thanks for something helpful: returning your notebook. This is not a request for directions.

scenario: You accidentally bump into someone at the station.
secondaryScenario: Your teammate wins a competition.
hint: A brief apology after bumping into someone, not congratulations for winning.

scenario: A student says goodbye to a teacher after class.
secondaryScenario: A guest enters a home for the first time.
hint: A goodbye when parting after class, not a greeting when entering a home.

scenario: Everyone is ready to begin a meal.
secondaryScenario: Everyone has just finished eating.
hint: Said just before eating. Check whether the meal is beginning or already finished.

scenario: You thank the host after finishing a meal.
secondaryScenario: You introduce yourself to a new class.
hint: Thanks after a meal is finished, not an introduction to new classmates.

scenario: You tell your family you are leaving home.
secondaryScenario: You welcome someone who returned home.
hint: The speaker is leaving home and expects to return; they are not welcoming someone back.

scenario: You see a family member off at the door.
secondaryScenario: You return home and announce your arrival.
hint: Spoken by the person staying home to someone leaving, not by the person arriving.

scenario: You return home and greet your family.
secondaryScenario: You meet someone for the first time.
hint: Spoken by the person returning home, not someone meeting a stranger.

scenario: You welcome a family member home.
secondaryScenario: You ask a shopkeeper for help.
hint: Spoken to the family member who has returned, not to a shopkeeper for help.

scenario: You meet a new classmate for the first time.
secondaryScenario: You congratulate a friend on an award.
hint: A first introduction. Look for people meeting for the first time, not celebrating an award.

japanese: よろしくおねがいします
scenario: You finish introducing yourself to a new group.
secondaryScenario: You leave the office before coworkers.
hint: A friendly request for a good relationship after introducing yourself, not leaving work.

japanese: おめでとうございます
scenario: Your friend has won a school competition.
secondaryScenario: Your friend is feeling sick.
hint: Congratulations on an achievement, not words to someone who is ill.

scenario: You greet a teammate after practice.
secondaryScenario: You enter someone's home as a guest.
hint: Acknowledge a teammate’s effort after practice, not your arrival as a houseguest.

scenario: You politely ask a clerk for assistance.
secondaryScenario: You refuse an offer because you are fine.
hint: A polite request for assistance, not a refusal of help.

scenario: Someone offers help but you are okay.
secondaryScenario: You interrupt a teacher to ask a question.
hint: Reassure the person offering help that you are okay, not interrupt a teacher.

scenario: You enter the teacher's office politely.
secondaryScenario: You welcome a friend home.
hint: Politely acknowledge entering someone’s office, not welcome a person returning home.

scenario: You will see your classmate again tomorrow.
secondaryScenario: You meet a manager for the first time.
hint: A farewell that mentions seeing the person tomorrow, not a first meeting.

scenario: You leave work before your coworkers.
secondaryScenario: You arrive late and keep someone waiting.
hint: Acknowledge that you are leaving work while others remain, not arriving late.

scenario: You apologize after making someone wait.
secondaryScenario: You ask a guest to wait for a moment.
hint: The other person has already waited and you are now ready; you are not asking them to wait.

scenario: A staff member formally accepts a customer's request.
secondaryScenario: A friend casually agrees to play a game.
hint: Respectfully accept a customer’s request as staff, rather than casually agree with a friend.

scenario: A receptionist asks a visitor to wait briefly.
secondaryScenario: A doctor tells a patient to take care.
hint: Ask a visitor to wait a little longer, not wish a sick person well.

scenario: You tell a friend to travel safely.
secondaryScenario: You enter a host's home.
hint: Wish someone safety as they travel, not announce that you are entering a home.

scenario: You speak to someone who is ill.
secondaryScenario: You greet a coworker after a shift.
hint: Wish an ill person a good recovery, not thank a coworker for their work.

scenario: You enter a friend's home as a guest.
secondaryScenario: You finish eating at a restaurant.
hint: A guest acknowledges entering someone else’s home, not finishing a meal.

scenario: You apologize after making a formal mistake.
secondaryScenario: You welcome a returning family member.
hint: Apologize for an action that already happened, not welcome someone home.

japanese: どうぞよろしくお願いいたします
scenario: You close a formal self-introduction.
secondaryScenario: You ask for the restaurant bill.
hint: A respectful closing to a self-introduction, not a request to pay for food.

scenario: You sincerely apologize to a customer.
secondaryScenario: You congratulate a close friend.
hint: A sincere apology for a customer-facing mistake, not congratulations.

scenario: You offer to help someone carrying boxes.
secondaryScenario: You ask permission to take a photo.
hint: Offer your own help with a task such as carrying boxes; you are not asking permission.

scenario: You thank someone whose help solved your problem.
secondaryScenario: You ask someone to repeat a sentence.
hint: Recognize that someone’s help solved your problem, not ask them to repeat their words.

scenario: A staff member guides a guest to a seat.
secondaryScenario: A traveler asks for directions.
hint: The speaker invites a guest to come this way, rather than asks where to go.

japanese: もう一度お願いします
scenario: You politely ask someone to repeat what they said.
secondaryScenario: You tell a coworker to travel safely.
hint: Ask to hear the same words again, not wish someone a safe trip.

japanese: 写真を撮ってもいいですか
romaji: Shashin o totte mo ii desu ka
scenario: You ask permission before taking a photo.
secondaryScenario: You announce that you are leaving home.
hint: Ask permission before taking a picture, not announce your departure.

scenario: You tell restaurant staff you have a reservation.
secondaryScenario: You apologize for bumping into someone.
hint: Tell staff about a booking already made, not apologize for an accident.

japanese: お会計をお願いします
scenario: You politely ask for the bill after a meal.
secondaryScenario: You introduce yourself to a new group.
hint: Ask to pay after eating, not introduce yourself to a group.

scenario: A staff member offers to guide a visitor.
secondaryScenario: A guest thanks the cook after eating.
hint: The speaker offers to lead a visitor, not thank the person who cooked.

scenario: You meet someone after a long absence.
secondaryScenario: You meet someone for the first time.
hint: You already know this person but have not met for a long time; it is not a first meeting.

scenario: You end a polite conversation and expect to meet again.
secondaryScenario: You begin a meal with your host.
hint: A light, polite goodbye with an expectation of meeting again, not a mealtime phrase.

japanese: 恐れ入りますが、もう一度お願いします
scenario: You ask a senior client to repeat an important point.
secondaryScenario: You casually ask a close friend to repeat a joke.
hint: Ask for repetition with extra respect toward a senior client, rather than casually ask a friend.

scenario: You make a formal apology to a customer.
secondaryScenario: You thank a friend for returning a pencil.
hint: A very formal apology to a customer, not thanks for returning an item.

scenario: You formally confirm a supervisor's instructions.
secondaryScenario: You casually agree with a sibling.
hint: Respectfully confirm that you understand a supervisor’s instructions, not casual agreement at home.

japanese: お手数をおかけします
scenario: You acknowledge that your request creates extra work.
secondaryScenario: You celebrate a classmate's achievement.
hint: Acknowledge the extra trouble caused by your request, not celebrate someone’s achievement.

japanese: ご確認いただけますでしょうか
scenario: You politely ask a manager to review a document.
secondaryScenario: You tell a friend to view a funny photo.
hint: Respectfully ask a manager to check something, not casually show a friend a funny picture.

japanese: 伺ってもよろしいでしょうか
scenario: You respectfully ask whether you may visit.
secondaryScenario: You ask a close friend where lunch is.
hint: Humbly ask permission to visit someone, not ask a friend where lunch is.

japanese: お目にかかれて光栄です
scenario: You meet a distinguished guest for the first time.
secondaryScenario: You greet a classmate seen every day.
hint: Express that meeting a distinguished guest is an honor, not an everyday classmate greeting.

japanese: ご配慮いただきありがとうございます
scenario: You thank a supervisor for thoughtful consideration.
secondaryScenario: You say goodbye to a shop clerk.
hint: Thank someone for thoughtful consideration of your needs, not say goodbye.

japanese: 先ほどは失礼いたしました
scenario: You formally apologize for your earlier behavior.
secondaryScenario: You begin a casual call with a friend.
hint: Apologize respectfully for something you did earlier, not start a friendly call.

japanese: お忙しいところ申し訳ありません
scenario: You interrupt a busy professor with an important request.
secondaryScenario: You welcome a family member home.
hint: Acknowledge interrupting someone who is busy before making your request, not welcome someone home.

japanese: 何卒よろしくお願いいたします
scenario: You close a very formal request.
secondaryScenario: You ask a friend to pass the salt.
hint: A very respectful closing asking for cooperation with your request, not a casual request at the table.

japanese: ご無沙汰しております
scenario: You greet a senior person after a long absence.
secondaryScenario: You greet someone met yesterday.
hint: A humble greeting to someone senior after a long time apart, not someone you saw yesterday.

japanese: お招きいただきありがとうございます
scenario: You thank a host for a formal invitation.
secondaryScenario: You ask a waiter for the bill.
hint: Thank your host specifically for inviting you, not request the restaurant bill.

scenario: You politely tell a host not to go to extra trouble.
secondaryScenario: You warn a traveler about weather.
hint: Gently reassure your host that extra effort is unnecessary, not warn someone about weather.

japanese: お先に失礼いたします
scenario: You formally leave before senior colleagues.
secondaryScenario: You leave a casual picnic with friends.
hint: A formal workplace farewell when you leave before senior coworkers, not a casual picnic goodbye.

japanese: ご足労いただきありがとうございます
scenario: You thank a guest for traveling to meet you.
secondaryScenario: You thank a friend for an eraser.
hint: Thank someone specifically for making the journey to see you, not lending a small item.

japanese: 差し支えなければ、お名前を伺えますか
romaji: Sashitsukae nakereba, onamae o ukagaemasu ka
scenario: You politely request a visitor's name.
secondaryScenario: You call a best friend by a nickname.
hint: Ask a visitor’s name politely and indirectly, not call a friend by a name you already know.

japanese: もう少し詳しくお聞かせください
scenario: You respectfully invite a client to explain further.
secondaryScenario: You command a sibling to speak faster.
hint: Respectfully invite more detail about what was said, not demand faster speech.

japanese: 引き続きよろしくお願いいたします
scenario: You close a meeting and request continued cooperation.
secondaryScenario: You say good night to family.
hint: Request continued cooperation after a professional meeting, not say good night at home.

japanese: 貴重なお時間をいただき、ありがとうございます
romaji: Kichou na ojikan o itadaki, arigatou gozaimasu
scenario: You thank an executive for meeting with you.
secondaryScenario: You thank a classmate for a quick greeting.
hint: Thank someone for giving their valuable time to meet you, not for a passing greeting.
